correctness.rationale: Full frozen RESULT.md proof yields Sdot=S(1-Sq) and pdot_i=-S p_i((Ap)_i-q)+mu(1-d p_i). Symmetry ensures Phi_S=1/S-q and Phi_pi=-2S(Ap)_i+2mu/p_i, giving the exact positive metric sum-of-squares. Entrywise A>0 bounds Phi above by log S-mS, while positive mutation logarithms exclude simplex boundary, so positive superlevels are compact. Real-analytic gradient convergence via Lojasiewicz yields convergence to one equilibrium even with multistability, not necessarily same equilibrium for all initial points. Independently evaluated a rational d=3 asymmetric-in-state example with A diagonal 1/off-diagonal 13/10, mu=3/100; both Phi derivative and squares equal 1008907/1620000 exactly. The full general result is based on the analytic proof, not that one test.
